business: SEGMENT: PI car accident intake, Pleasanton (Shotland pilot)
prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but “which lawyer” depends on the details of your crash and what matters most to you (trial experience, settlement speed, cost, language, rating). A practical way to proceed is to (A) know what to look for, (B) ask the right questions when you interview lawyers, and (C) get a few free consultations to compare. Below is a concise guide and some next steps.

Key things I need to know (or that a lawyer will ask)
- Where and when did the crash occur? (Pleasanton, CA — date/time)
- How severe are your injuries? Any hospital visits, ongoing care, or permanent impairment?
- Was anyone cited? Do you have the police report?
- Are there witnesses or photos/video of the crash?
- Are you being contacted by an insurance company? Have you given a recorded statement?
- Are you covered by health insurance, Medi-Cal, Medicare, or PIP?
- How long since the crash? (Important for deadlines)

Important immediate actions
- Get medical treatment and follow-up. Your health and the medical record are critical to the claim.
- Preserve evidence: photos, videos, police report, bills, repair estimates, names/contacts of witnesses.
- Don’t give a recorded statement to the other driver’s insurer without consulting a lawyer.
- Keep a log of pain, treatment, missed work, and expenses.

What kind of lawyer to hire
- Specialization: Look for a personal injury attorney who handles car crashes and has substantial experience in auto-accident cases.
- Trial vs. settlement experience: If the other side denies fault or lowballs offers, you want someone comfortable going to trial.
- Local familiarity: A Pleasanton or Alameda County attorney will know the local court, judges, and defense firms.
- Communication and team: Ask who will actually handle your file (attorney vs. paralegal) and how often you’ll get updates.
- Fee structure: Most PI lawyers work on contingency (no recovery, no fee). Typical contingency fees in CA are about 33%–40% plus case costs; get this in writing.

CA-specific legal points to know
- Statute of limitations: In California you generally have 2 years from the date of injury to file a personal injury lawsuit (C.C.P. § 335.1). Missing this can bar your claim.
- Comparative negligence: California uses “pure comparative negligence,” so you can recover proportionally even if you were partly at fault.
- Government defendants: If a government vehicle was involved, different/shorter notice deadlines may apply.

Questions to ask at a consultation
- How many car-accident cases do you handle yearly? How many do you settle vs. go to trial?
- What is your track record with cases like mine (injury severity, liability issues)?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day? How will we communicate and how often?
- What is your fee and how are costs handled? If we don’t recover, do I owe anything?
- How long do you expect this case to take? What range of outcomes is realistic?
- Can you provide references or client testimonials? Have you handled cases in Alameda County courts?
- Do you handle Medicare/Medicaid liens or subrogation issues?

How to choose
- Interview 2–4 attorneys for free consultations (most PI lawyers offer this).
- Compare experience, costs, communication style, and how they value your case.
- Verify license and discipline history at the State Bar of California (calbar.ca.gov).
- Read reviews and ask for sample case results, but judge more on fit and experience than just ratings.

Where to find attorneys
- Start with the Alameda County Bar Association lawyer-referral service or the State Bar of California “Find a Lawyer” tool.
- If you want, I can search for Pleasanton-area personal injury lawyers and provide a short list (with contact info and practice focus). Tell me whether you prefer trial attorneys, bilingual lawyers, or any other preference.

If you’d like, tell me a few more details about your crash (when, injuries, whether you’ve seen a doctor, if you’ve talked to insurers) and I’ll: (1) recommend what to prioritize, and (2) pull a short list of local lawyers you can call for a free consult. Which would you like me to do?
